reason: Butler mode's thread transcript, its live answer and the chat pop-up passed answers to bare ReactMarkdown, so GFM tables used browser defaults (centred headers, no borders) and inherited overflow-wrap:anywhere, which collapsed columns and split short values. A shared ButlerMarkdown component wraps each table in a focusable, bordered scroll region with start-aligned headers, row dividers, normal word wrapping, a minimum Item column and minimum short columns, plus code/pre/list styling. The butler-mode Playwright area now also covers ButlerChatPopup and ButlerMarkdown.
exclusions: No Core change, so no Python tests. Other Butler surfaces (side panel NebulaControlAssistant, Ask Nebula) already style tables or are untouched. Playwright runs the butler-mode real-Core journey on desktop, compact, Chromium 390 and WebKit 390; the 320/430 profiles add no table-specific geometry beyond 390.
